question: Is there a named owner for the platform who can approve AI access? (Links to RACI "CRM platform owner".)
Which product and version runs in production, and is it within vendor support? Unsupported versions limit what security fixes and API features you can rely on.
How much of the platform is customized (scripts, workflows, custom objects)? Where is the customization documented? AI integrations built on undocumented custom logic break at upgrades.
Is there a non-production environment that matches production closely enough to test AI integrations, with masked data (SAF-11)?
Is an upgrade or migration planned in the next 12-18 months? If yes, decide whether the AI integration waits for it, or is built so it can move with it.
For the fields the use case needs: how complete are they, and how current? Sample 50 records and count.
Are there duplicate customer records? Is there a rule for which record is the "golden" one?
Are reference values (product codes, status codes, categories) consistent, or do several codes mean the same thing?

Free-text fields (notes, comments, transcripts): what do staff actually write there? Sample them. Expect personal details, payment data or passwords typed in by mistake; this decides masking (SAF-19).
Are there known data-quality issues already tracked? Link them.

question: Where does CPNI live? List the objects and fields with call detail, services subscribed, usage and billing detail. Ask counsel which of them are CPNI under 47 CFR s.64.2003 ([CPNI]).

question: Are customer CPNI approval or opt-out choices stored, reliable and machine-readable, so an AI use case can respect them ([CPNI] s.64.2007)?

question: Are there data-location or contract limits that stop data leaving a country or a cloud?
User interface (staff and customer portals)
Official APIs or web services: which exist, what authentication they support (OAuth, tokens, basic auth, session-based), and whether they enforce the CRM's own visibility rules
Direct database access: who has it, with which accounts? AI must not use it (SAF-02).
Reporting replicas, data warehouses and data lakes: how fresh, which access rules apply? A copy without the CRM's visibility rules is a common way to over-share with AI.
Batch exports, import/export tools and file transfers: where do files land, who can read them, how long do they stay?
Which path will the AI use, and does it apply the field allowlist and the user's visibility?

Is there a complete list of integrations (inbound and outbound, real-time and batch, middleware, scheduled jobs, file flows, scripts)? Large CRM estates often have more than anyone remembers; search schedulers, middleware configs and server cron tables, not only documents.
For each: owner, direction, protocol, authentication method, account used, data objects, schedule, monitoring.
Which integrations use shared or highly privileged accounts? Plan to split them before adding AI (SAF-01).
Where are integration credentials stored? Config files, scripts and database tables with clear-text passwords are common in older estates; move them to a secrets manager (SAF-05).
Which existing integrations will the AI use case touch or depend on?
Can the platform give a non-human identity its own limited role, or do all integrations run as one user?

Does the platform support modern authentication for APIs (for example OAuth 2.0 client credentials or token exchange)? If not, put a gateway or API layer in front that does, and keep the legacy credential inside it.
Can the platform log reads, not only writes? If not, log at the API or gateway layer (SAF-15).
Does the platform support current TLS versions and certificate validation on all integration endpoints?
Is there performance headroom? AI features can add many small queries; test load in non-production.
Are business rules enforced in the application layer (so an AI write through the API is validated), or only in the user interface?
Can changes be rolled back? Is the audit trail enabled for the objects AI would change (SAF-22)?
Are staff accounts in the CRM linked to the central directory (SSO), so an assistant acting for a user can carry that user's identity (SAF-03)?
Are leavers removed from the CRM on time?
Are CRM audit logs sent to the central log platform?
Can you tell, from logs, which records a given integration account read last week?
Is there monitoring and alerting for the platform and its integrations, with a named on-call?
Is there a change process with maintenance windows and a rollback step?
Is there a tested backup and restore for the objects an AI feature may change?
Is there a manual process the business can fall back to if the AI feature is off (SAF-24)?
